beats.narration: If the Moon disappeared tonight, the biggest change wouldn't be in the sky... it would be in the ocean.

shots.scene_description: Moon vanishing from the night sky
Ocean waves under a moonless sky

beats.narration: The Moon's gravity pulls on our seas, creating the tides. Without it, the tides would shrink to about a third of their size.

shots.scene_description: Earth with the Moon pulling an ocean bulge
Tide gauge dropping to one third

beats.narration: Beaches and rock pools that depend on the tides would change forever, and lots of sea creatures living there would struggle.

shots.scene_description: Rock pool with a crab and starfish drying out

beats.narration: Nights would get much darker too. No moonlight at all... just stars.

shots.scene_description: Pitch black night with only stars

beats.narration: That's a big problem for animals. Corals use the full moon as a signal to release their eggs, all at the same time.

shots.scene_description: Coral reef releasing eggs under a full moon

beats.narration: And you could say goodbye to total solar eclipses. There'd be nothing to block the Sun.
Even our calendars would feel strange. The word month actually comes from the word moon!
Over millions of years, Earth's tilt could start to wobble without the Moon to steady it, causing wild, extreme seasons.

shots.scene_description: Summer and winter extremes split screen

beats.narration: But here's the crazy part. The Moon actually is leaving us, right now.

shots.scene_description: Moon slowly drifting away from Earth

beats.narration: It drifts about four centimetres further away every year. That's roughly as fast as your fingernails grow.

shots.scene_description: Fingernail growing next to a ruler

beats.narration: Don't worry though. It'll be around for billions of years. So go and enjoy the view tonight.
